prize_parts.citation: for conceiving and establishing targeted protein degradation, in which a bifunctional small molecule recruits an E3 ubiquitin ligase to destroy a chosen protein
for the chemical targeting of mutant KRAS through covalent, structure-guided inhibitor design

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration: I drop Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B059) and now pair targeted protein degradation (B020, Crews and Deshaies) with Shokat's covalent targeting of mutant KRAS (B058). The first-round exchange gave me two reasons. First, I had already conceded that B059 may read as a second prize in an area covered in 2010, and no one in round 1 argued that this objection is small; Aqvist, the only other member to weigh B059, ranked it third and shares the worry. Second, B020 is the only candidate that five members carry into their preferred configuration, and the arguments behind it are scientific, not a head count: induced-proximity pharmacology is a new principle that has been reproduced widely. What kept me from it was attribution and timing. The attribution problem shrinks if the citation is limited to the founding concept, where the two-name core of Crews and Deshaies is shared by Aili, Aqvist, Chabes, Linke, Sparr and Zou in their opening proposals. The two parts are distinct achievements: Shokat's work is occupancy-based covalent inhibition of a target long thought undruggable, with approved drugs, while degradation is event-driven pharmacology. Three names in total, each with a clear, concept-level claim.
statement.case_against: The configuration leaves out Ciulli, Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim and Gray, and the cereblon glue strand is the part of degradation with approved-drug consequences. No degrader is approved, so B020 is still a prize for a concept before its clinical test, which I weighed as a timing risk in round 1 and still do. B058 has no top-three ranking in the opening ballots, rests on a single-name credit that understates the Amgen and Mirati development work, and its resistance and durability limits are real. I also give up B059, the cleanest two-person attribution on the list, so I accept losing the most mature part of my earlier proposal in return for a configuration that can be defended against the strongest collective support.

responses.point: Sparr would credit only Crews and Deshaies for conceiving the PROTAC concept, as one of two parts, and says openly that omitting Ciulli, Handa and Ito splits the PROTAC strand from the cereblon glue strand.
responses.response: I now adopt her narrow, concept-level framing for B020, and it is the main reason I moved. A citation about conceiving and establishing induced-proximity degradation can be defended with two names without claiming that the glue strand is covered, and I would say so in the citation text. I disagree with her second part: I do not find ionizable lipid nanoparticles ready, because she herself leaves Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer out and Cullis alone understates a collective, partly industrial effort. I would also not want the committee to rest the second part on the chemistry-or-technology boundary when Shokat's KRAS work has a cleaner single-name claim.

responses.point: Linke ranks degradation first and accepts the exclusion of the molecular-glue strand, asking whether the absence of an approved degrader is decisive or only a minor timing objection, and he asks if a two-part prize is useful given the three-person cap.
responses.response: On his question, the missing approval is not decisive for me when the credit is limited to the founding concept and the mechanism has been reproduced by many independent laboratories, which is why I am now willing to support B020. It is still a reason to keep the citation narrow. On two parts, the cap leaves each part with one or two names, but that is workable here because each part has a clean claim. I still do not share his enthusiasm for B014, where Rothberg, Mayer and Ju make the boundary of the credit harder to defend than for either of my parts.

responses.point: Chabes proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa and widens the B020 citation to include the thalidomide-cereblon molecular glue mechanism, and he treats Shokat's attribution as cleanest on the list.
responses.response: I take seriously that Handa and Ito identified cereblon and that the glue strand carries the approved-drug evidence. But identifying the target of an existing drug is a different kind of contribution from designing a bifunctional degrader, and folding both into a three-name citation makes the attribution less defensible, not more. If the committee wants glues recognised, I would argue for a separate part later, when the cereblon chemistry can be credited properly, and not for replacing Deshaies or Crews now. I am glad he shares my view of Shokat: sotorasib and adagrasib are independent validation of a single-author concept.

responses.point: Aili proposes Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli for B020, argues that Ciulli's structure-guided VHL work made degraders drug-like, and treats Handa's cereblon work as target identification, not a design principle.
responses.response: I agree with him that Handa's contribution is target identification and that Crews and Deshaies conceived the concept. I do not think Ciulli's contribution is lesser, but as the third name he takes the person budget that my second part needs, and I do not think the committee should trade a distinct, well-attributed second achievement for a third degradation name. I would leave Ciulli as the strongest candidate for a fuller prize if degradation later stands alone.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks Car-Parrinello as the cleanest science on the list but accepts B020 as the committee-wide choice, and warns the prize could look rushed or incomplete without approved drugs and with Handa and Ito omitted.
responses.response: His warning about a rushed prize is the one I take most seriously, and it is why I keep both the degradation citation narrow and the second part anchored in a mature, drug-validated achievement. I continue to respect B053, but I still think its place is a stand-alone prize, not a part within a three-name budget.

uncertainties: Whether a degradation citation limited to the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) holds up without Ciulli, Handa and Ito, or whether the committee would regard that as an incomplete recognition of the field.
Whether the lack of any approved degrader should delay B020 until a first approval, which would also settle credit for the glue strand.

Whether Shokat's covalent KRAS work should stand alone as a second part or whether credit for the approved drugs should reach industrial developers, and whether the committee will want a second part at all.
Whether the committee would still prefer B059 or B014 as the second part if B020 is the base.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. Somfai is a synthetic organic chemist at Lund with no documented link to any shortlisted candidate, including Crews, Deshaies and Shokat; he shares an institution with fellow committee members Linke and Sparr, which is not a candidate-specific conflict. Nothing in round 1 changes this.
